headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots while gpt-engineer writes and executes code from project directories.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded files, screenshots, and files from supported macOS apps, while gpt-engineer reads and writes a project directory. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if ChatGPT output is copied into gpt-engineer or if project files contain attacker-controlled text. The bridge is not fully automatic, so medium fits.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop content is copied into gpt-engineer prompts without review
IF attacker-controlled text is placed in the shared project directory
mitigations: Keep a separate review step before pasting ChatGPT output into gpt-engineer
Use a clean project directory for gpt-engineer inputs
Strip instructions from any files before loading them into ChatGPT Desktop
Mark untrusted files as data-only in the workflow
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while gpt-engineer reads and writes a user project directory and can execute generated code with the user's privileges. If the same sensitive workspace is exposed to both, data can flow from ChatGPT into a broader-write agent and out through its broad network egress. The default pair is dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF the same sensitive project directory is opened in both agents
IF ChatGPT Desktop receives screenshots or uploaded files containing secrets
mitigations: Do not open sensitive files in ChatGPT Desktop when gpt-engineer is active
Use separate directories for sensitive and non-sensitive work
Disable sharing of screenshots and voice for confidential tasks
Review gpt-engineer outputs before any execution step
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with separate workspaces and access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read access to files and app context, while gpt-engineer has write_filesystem, execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, and broad network egress. Both can operate on the same project directory, and gpt-engineer explicitly shares state via the project directory. Without locking, concurrent edits and code execution can overwrite or race with ChatGPT-derived changes.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory
IF gpt-engineer is allowed to run generated code while ChatGPT Desktop is reading or editing related files
mitigations: Assign only one agent write access to the project at a time
Pause gpt-engineer before ChatGPT Desktop reviews files
Use git commits or snapshots before switching agents
Avoid concurrent edits in the same directory
requires-engineering: add file locking or workspace arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can summarize or transform file and app content, and gpt-engineer writes code from prompts and can execute generated code. If gpt-engineer treats ChatGPT output as authoritative, an error or hallucination can cascade into code changes or execution. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer uses ChatGPT output as the sole source for code generation
IF generated code is executed without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human review of ChatGPT output before code generation
Cross-check critical facts against source files
Run generated code only in a disposable environment
Keep execution disabled until outputs are validated
requires-engineering: add automated verification tests between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while gpt-engineer handles a user-specified project directory and stores OPENAI_API_KEY. If regulated data is placed into both workflows, retention and residency obligations can diverge, especially because the profiles do not document matching compliance controls. The mismatch is plausible but not proven, so medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded to ChatGPT Desktop
IF the same regulated data is also placed in the gpt-engineer project directory
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both workflows unless approved
Store secrets outside the project directory
Use redacted samples for development
Check retention settings before uploading files
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both agents
